records.rationale: Retain the clamp of the unsigned RLIMIT_NICE value to 40 before signed conversion and subtraction. Configured Rust Binder Thread::do_set_priority calls this method for a fair-policy task without CAP_SYS_NICE. RLIM_INFINITY or an arbitrary high raw limit otherwise permits signed subtraction overflow and a kernel panic with Rust overflow checks. Values 1..40 map to nice 19..-20; zero maps to 20 and the Binder caller rejects it as unset. Limits above 40 grant no priority beyond the legal minimum nice. This is a concrete safety fix for the selected Android priority API; native LTS scheduler checks are not weakened by this change.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust publication, poll and priority helpers
records.subject: ANDROID: rust: fix overflow in rlimit_nice()

records.rationale: Retain module! imports_ns parsing and import_ns modinfo emission, positively consumed by the configured WrapFD module for DMA_BUF. It uses the existing ASCII string-array parser and escaped byte-string modinfo emitter for both built-in and loadable modules. The built SDK modules.builtin.modinfo contains wrapfd.import_ns=DMA_BUF. This preserves native modpost namespace checking rather than bypassing it, and is generic module source infrastructure, not historical binary KMI.

records.rationale: Retain SetOnce used by Rust Binder process poll queues and transaction logs. Exactly one successful 0->1 atomic compare-exchange owns initialization; a Release store publishes state 2 and Acquire readers only then borrow initialized data. Losing populate calls drop their unused input, and exclusive Drop only destroys the initialized value. Binder poll allocates outside its node_refs lock, serializes population and re-reads the published queue; transaction logging tolerates an unpopulated container. The complete selected implementation matches ACK; no native LTS atomic implementation is replaced.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust publication, poll and priority helpers

records.rationale: Retain SetOnce Send only for T:Send and Sync only for T:Send+Sync. The bounds cover both shared references returned to readers and movement/destruction of an inserted value on another thread. These are required by the selected shared Binder process/log containers; the atomic publication protocol is reviewed with f4bf2ca6bd07. Do not treat atomic initialization alone as sufficient for arbitrary non-Sync payloads.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust publication, poll and priority helpers

records.rationale: Retain PollCondVarBox with an embedded RCU callback head for the configured Rust Binder process poll queue. The box remains pinned, manually transfers its unique allocation on drop, wakes/removes poll waiters via native __wake_up_pollfree, then defers reclamation through native kvfree_call_rcu. It deliberately replaces the synchronous PollCondVar destructor while preserving its required grace period; CondVar has no additional owning resource destructor to skip. This also permits dropping a losing SetOnce population while the Binder node_refs spinlock is held, without synchronize_rcu sleeping there. The non-null embedded callback head avoids the native headless might_sleep path. Ordinary PollCondVar retains synchronous destruction. Native LTS RCU freeing and waitqueue wake implementation remain; actual epoll/RCU races have not been executed.
evidence: SECURITY.md: Rust publication, poll and priority helpers

scope: Full five candidate patches; complete SetOnce and PollCondVarBox implementations; selected task clamp and caller; module namespace parser/emitter and WrapFD declaration; native waitqueue/RCU reclamation and CondVar fields examined. Other task priority, module-parameter and whole-driver changes are independently audited.
